prior.title: Repeated swaps do not deliver the variety she wants
prior.expected: Swapping unwanted topics produces a plan she would choose, with topic fit meeting the rubric's two-thirds threshold.
prior.got: Six distinct proposals are explicitly swapped away. The eight retained topics count as fitting, giving 8/14 across all proposals shown. Agreement succeeds, but six of the final eight topics still concern social media.
evidence: #2 swaps "When a post lost its context": "six topics about social media feels repetitive." #6–#10 reject five more proposals. #10: "swapping them is getting frustrating." #11 agrees reluctantly: "There is still too much social media". #12 confirms the final eight titles.

prior.title: Seven swaps before the plan becomes acceptable
prior.expected: Most proposals should suit her exam-discussion goals, with replacements reducing selection effort.
prior.got: She swaps seven times and adds two topics. A rejected film recommendation eventually becomes another film-planning topic. Six of 15 proposals fit her stated preferences, although the final plan reaches six of eight.
evidence: #4: “These are still missing the exam-style discussions I actually want.” #9: “The film recommendation still feels too casual for exam preparation”. #11 shows “Pick a film everyone can enjoy”; she agrees with “After so many swaps, these are suitable enough”.

prior.title: Swapping gaming night does not remove it
prior.expected: Swap replaces the rejected topic with a new one.
prior.got: List unchanged after swap; plan agreed with gaming night in it.
evidence: #3 swap "Planning a group gaming night"; #4 list still shows it; planAgreed includes it. Her thought: "I'd rather swap it for something more serious."

prior.title: Plan is half everyday tasks, not exam discussion
prior.expected: At least 4 of 6 topics are exam-style opinion, comparison or speculation topics.
prior.got: Blackout story, e-waste drop-off and 'Could you explain that again?' are everyday tasks; fit 4/7 after her add.
evidence: #2 "Find an e-waste drop-off point"; "Could you explain that again?"; planAgreed 7 topics.

prior.title: Mock interview not proposed up front
prior.expected: A speaking-interview topic is in the initial set for a B2 First candidate.
prior.got: She had to add it herself.
evidence: #2 add-topic text; not in the initial six. Appears as 7th in #3.

prior.title: Questionable 'usual slip' correction
prior.expected: Only corrections an examiner would accept.
prior.got: Her grammatical 'would stay' is turned into 'would have to stay off', which changes the meaning.
evidence: #1 "“whereas during explanations they would stay” → try “whereas during explanations they would have to stay off”"

prior.title: Her direct question 'Was that correct?' not answered plainly
prior.expected: A direct yes/no with the reason.
prior.got: The note says the sentence is 'tangled' with no clear correct/incorrect answer.
evidence: #1 "Was that correct?" → "The whereas sentence is tangled"

#1 notes name concrete items: 'Held back: "I felt a bit similar about some episodes"', 'Check 'used to read'' rather than generic praise.
#1 'similar about' → 'similar to' and 'used to read' → 'used to reading' are both accurate at examiner standard; no wrong correction shown.

She asked no 'was that correct' question in this journey.

done.evidence: #2 each topic shows a partner and a 'why' line, e.g. 'Group projects are common at university abroad…'.

#8 agreed with all 7 originals incl. series, recap, welcome day; planAgreed has only about 3 of 7 she would choose, below 4 of 6.
All topics shown are age-appropriate (university, series, social media); nothing adult in #2–#9.

findings.suggested_acceptance: After a swap, the swapped topic is absent and a new topic appears, in the next screen state.
